steps.title: Import React and styled-components
steps.instruction: Import React from 'react' and styled from 'styled-components' at the top of your file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the styled function from their respective packages.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and styled-components here

// Your component code will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have the necessary imports for creating styled components with TypeScript.
successCriteria: The code must include two import statements: one for React from 'react' and one for styled from 'styled-components'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and styled-components. These are the foundational packages needed to create styled components in TypeScript.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but you need both imports. Make sure you're importing React from 'react' and styled from 'styled-components'.
steps.feedbackWrong: This step requires importing React and styled-components. Check that you're using the correct import syntax and package names.

steps.title: Create a styled button component
steps.instruction: Create a styled button component named StyledButton using styled.button`` syntax. Place it after the imports and before any other component code.
steps.hint: Use styled.button followed by backticks to create a styled button component. Remember to export it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A StyledButton component is created using styled.button`` syntax with basic styling properties.
successCriteria: Contains at least one CSS property
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created your first styled component using styled.button`` syntax.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using styled.button`` syntax and exporting the component.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a StyledButton component using styled.button`` syntax with some basic CSS properties.

steps.title: Add basic styling to the button
steps.instruction: Inside your StyledButton component, add basic CSS properties: padding, background color, border, and border-radius.
steps.hint: Add CSS properties inside the template literal after the styled.button`` call. Use properties like padding, background-color, border, and border-radius.
steps.expectedOutcome: The StyledButton component will have basic visual styling with padding, background color, border, and rounded corners.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added basic styling to your button component with padding, background color, border, and border-radius.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure to include all four properties: padding, background-color, border, and border-radius.
steps.feedbackWrong: The StyledButton component doesn't have the required CSS properties. Add padding, background-color, border, and border-radius inside the template literal.

steps.title: Create a styled container component
steps.instruction: Create a Container component using styled.div``. This will be a styled div element for layout purposes.
steps.hint: Use the styled.div template literal syntax to create a new styled component named Container.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a styled container component
const Container = styled.div``;
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a Container component created using styled.div``, ready to receive styling in the next step.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a Container component using styled.div``. This gives you a styled div element that you can use for layout in your application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're creating a component named Container using styled.div``. Check that you're using the correct syntax with the backticks.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to create a Container component using styled.div``. Remember to use the styled.div template literal syntax.

steps.title: Style the container component
steps.instruction: Add layout styling to the Container component. Use the styled-components template literal to set display: flex, flex-direction: column, align-items: center, and padding: 2rem.
steps.hint: Inside the empty template literal for Container, write CSS properties like you would in a regular CSS rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Container component will have flexbox layout styling applied, making it ready to center child components.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added layout styling to the Container component. The flexbox properties will help center and arrange child elements.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but some styling properties are missing. Make sure to include all four: display: flex, flex-direction: column, align-items: center, and padding: 2rem.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Container component doesn't have the required styling. Remember to add CSS properties inside the template literal for the Container.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns JSX. This will be your main component.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. The component should return a JSX element (like a <div>).
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an App component defined that returns JSX.
successCriteria: The App component is defined as a function (or arrow function) and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component. This will serve as the main entry point for your styled components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your App component is properly defined and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't defined correctly. Ensure you create a function named App that returns JSX.

steps.title: Add Container to App component
steps.instruction: In your App component, return the Container component as the root element.
steps.hint: The Container component should wrap all the content you'll eventually add inside it. For now, just return it as a JSX element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now returns the Container component as its root JSX element.
successCriteria: Container component is returned from App
Container is used as a JSX element
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the Container component to your App. This establishes the layout foundation for your styled component pattern.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning the Container component as JSX from the App component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Container component needs to be returned from the App component. Check that you're using it as a JSX element.

steps.title: Add StyledButton to App component
steps.instruction: Inside the Container component in your App component, add the StyledButton component.
steps.hint: Place the StyledButton component as a child element inside the Container's opening and closing tags.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now renders the Container with the StyledButton inside it.
successCriteria: StyledButton component is placed inside Container component
App component returns JSX with both components
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the StyledButton component inside the Container. This demonstrates how styled components can be composed together in your UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the StyledButton is placed directly inside the Container component's JSX tags.
steps.feedbackWrong: The StyledButton component should be added as a child element inside the Container component in the App component's return statement.

steps.title: Add button text content
steps.instruction: Add text content like 'Click me!' to the StyledButton component inside your App component.
steps.hint: Inside the StyledButton JSX element, add text content between the opening and closing tags.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding text content to a button component
<button>Click me!</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The StyledButton component will display text content when rendered.
successCriteria: The StyledButton component should contain text content (like 'Click me!') between its opening and closing tags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added text content to the StyledButton component. This makes the button visible and interactive for users.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added text content directly inside the StyledButton component's JSX tags.
steps.feedbackWrong: The StyledButton component doesn't appear to have text content. Add text like 'Click me!' between the opening and closing tags of the StyledButton component.

steps.title: Add hover effect to button
steps.instruction: Add a hover effect to your StyledButton component using the &:hover pseudo-class selector inside the styled template literal.
steps.hint: Inside the styled.button template literal, add &:hover { background-color: ... } to change the button's background when hovered.
steps.expectedOutcome: The StyledButton component will have a hover effect that changes its background color when the mouse hovers over it.
successCriteria: hover selector includes a background-color property
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a hover effect to your styled button using the &:hover pseudo-class.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the &:hover selector inside the StyledButton template literal with a background-color property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hover effect wasn't added correctly. Check that you've added &:hover { background-color: ... } inside the StyledButton template literal.

steps.title: Add props interface to button
steps.instruction: Add a TypeScript interface named 'StyledButtonProps' above your StyledButton component. The interface should define a single property called 'primary' of type boolean.
steps.hint: Create an interface using the 'interface' keyword, then use it to type the props parameter of your styled component.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a TypeScript interface that defines the props your StyledButton component can accept, making it type-safe.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a TypeScript interface for your styled component props. This will enable type checking when you pass props to the component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your interface has the correct name (StyledButtonProps) and includes a 'primary' property of type boolean.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface wasn't created correctly. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword, name it 'StyledButtonProps', and include a 'primary: boolean' property.

steps.title: Use props in button styling
steps.instruction: Modify the StyledButton component to conditionally set its background color based on the primary prop. Use a template literal with a ternary operator that checks props.primary.
steps.hint: Inside the styled.button template literal, use ${props => props.primary ? 'color1' : 'color2'} to set the background-color property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The StyledButton component will have a background color that changes based on whether the primary prop is true or false.
successCriteria: StyledButton template literal contains background-color property
Conditionally sets color based on primary prop
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented conditional styling based on props. The button's background color will now change depending on whether the primary prop is true or false.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check if you've included the background-color property and used the correct ternary syntax with props.primary.
steps.feedbackWrong: The StyledButton component doesn't yet have conditional styling based on the primary prop. Try adding a background-color property with a ternary operator that checks props.primary.
